utterances.text: Well, I would say there were multiple causes, and I think I tried to identify some of the, I would say, chain of causation in the background report. The increasing failure of the interparty agreement to mediate or to serve as a mechanism for mediation between the political parties was a major cause of those rising tensions. The war in Croatia, which had a polarising influence on the parties in Bosnia, and of course in Croatia, was a major contributor to that. The movements for independence in Slovenia and Croatia and also Macedonia contributed to that. Certainly the arming of -- acquisition of arms by nationalist formations was also a major contributing factor. These, in my view, coincided with some longer term causal factors which in a sense were brought to a point of confrontation, particularly the taking of the census in April 1991 and the multi-party elections that produced such a decisive victory in most places for the nationalist parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you complete with your answer?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The causes that you've stated here, you obtained those and were able to formulate an opinion that those were the causes by the review of the binder that you have in front of you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I believe your question was related to the tensions throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Prijedor municipality in particular. So the documents that are here would form only a very small part of what I have reviewed over some years to identify those factors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that I understand, as one, I believe the third, but one of the causes of this increased tension from 1991 through the summer of 1992 was the movement of independence, as you say, of Slovenia, Croatia, and Macedonia. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes. These movements echoed in Bosnia in such a way that it increased tensions among the nationalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even though it was outside the republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They still had an enormous trickling effect within the entire region, and particularly in the Prijedor municipality. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I wouldn't identify the Prijedor municipality as being especially or extraordinarily influenced by those events, but would say they were influential in the increasing negative relations between the nationalist parties, in particular, throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in your report, you try to set for us a sort of timetable of when these certain events that were causing these tensions inside the Prijedor municipality, when they first started, when they ended. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well, I would agree with part of your statement. I think I did try to establish some points in time when they were -- when relations deteriorated. I don't know if I identified a single starting point or a terminal point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that there were other causes that may have contributed to the ever-increasing tensions in the Prijedor municipality that you haven't listed or is your list of causes exhaustive?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: There were certainly other causes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you know what a mujahedin fighter from Afghanistan is. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true, sir, that from your research analysis of the periodicals and newspaper articles that these fighters were actually in the region in 1991/1992?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I know of no such fighters in the region in 1991. I would certainly note there were some in the region, the broad region, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and northwest Bosnia, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, where did you obtain that information that there were such fighters in the broad region Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I can't give you a specific --

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: -- Source. It is a matter of record that has been attested to in probably hundreds of interviews and press reports from the time, some of which have, you know, appeared very recently, some of which appeared as early as 1992/1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name one of those sources for us?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time examine or study the number of mujahedin fighters who were in Bosnia-Herzegovina in, as you say, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who invited these fighters to come into Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. I really -- once again I have to interrupt you. As I mentioned before, we are not interested in any other crimes probably committed, prepared, or whatsoever in the region. I can't see the relevance for our concrete case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may respectfully reply, Mr. President, we believe that the introduction -- and I was getting to it -- to the precise in 1992 may have affected the tensions between the ethnic groups, thereby forcing, we believe, some to act in a certain manner that has been highly criticised by my learned friends at the Office of the Prosecution by acting in such a manner when in fact they were reactive measures that were taken to protect the sovereignty of what they believed was their country and portions thereof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Counsel, do you really want to make the point that the accused in this case, Dr. Milomir Stakic, acted in defence against fighters from Afghanistan at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may have leave to ask one more question on this issue, or I can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know, and in your report, do you not identify an entity known as the Bosnian Muslim Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, who are or who was the entity known as the Bosnian Muslim Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: The Green Berets were one of two paramilitary groups founded by the SDA in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say founded by the SDA, how do you reach such a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: The SDA held a meeting in June of 1991, a meeting which was reported in the press, and formed a national defence council. Subsequent to that, they also formed the -- or sponsored the formation of the Green Berets and the Patriotic League. The existence of both of those organisations and their gradual growth are chronicled in a number of memoirs by Bosnian Muslim or Bosniak military leaders. They are reported by -- in papers or presentations by Bosniak political leaders and are the subject of numerous interviews and press articles that have appeared in the period since 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that in June of 1991, the political party SDA formed a national defence council, correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, was the SDA the party which held the Presidency of the municipality of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Your question is not clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the republic level.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well, the Presidency of the socialist republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time had seven members; two members were from the SDS, two were from the HDZ, and three were members of the SDA. The president of the Presidency was Alija Izetbegovic of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that I'm correct, it wasn't the Presidency of the socialist republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina that voted and founded and formed this national defence council; it was the political party of the president of that Presidency. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, sir, June of 1991, did the SDS form any such national defence council?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true after reviewing the minutes of the SDS municipal board that, in fact, no such entity was founded by the SDS at the time of June 1991?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I find no reference to the creation of a party-controlled paramilitary group in the Prijedor SDS minutes. There is substantial discussion in those minutes about the arming of Serbs, the need for the JNA to support that process. But no formation of that group under the jurisdiction or aegis of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the national defence council a paramilitary group?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: It was a party organ. I don't think it was a paramilitary organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, the paramilitary organisations within the SDA subsequent to June of 1991 consisted of two entities; namely, the Bosnian Muslim Green Berets, and secondly the Patriotic League. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you obtained this information from your review of various newspaper accounts, articles, and journals for that time period. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: As I've indicated, I have seen -- learned of this from numerous newspaper articles that appeared after 1995. Several memoirs which speak of the creation and gradual growth of these organisations, and interviews, press interviews, that have, again, taken place principally since 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the HDZ, in June of 1991, establish a comparable entity such as the SDA's national defence council?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: The HDZ in Croatia did, indeed, have a body which would be, I think, comparable. The Croatian national guard, yet, operated principally in Croatia, but also on occasion operated in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the entity known as the national defence council which was formed by the SDA, did it have any active members?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm not too sure what you mean -- what the question means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it if you allow. Did, in June of 1991, the entity formed by the SDA called the national defence council, did it have any members?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I think it had a substantial number of members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was, if you know, the goal of this entity in June of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't recall what their stated goal was. They, in fact, issued a statement stating what their goal was, and I don't recall specifically how it was formulated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if that goal, from the national defence council, changed or evolved from its formation in June of 1991 through September of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, at the height of that organisation, what was its membership?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, when the entity identified as the national defence council ceased, if at all, to exist?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, as you sit here, you don't know whether or not it was even in existence in 1992, or do you?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well, I don't know specifically when it ceased to exist. I find no record of it operating after about April of 1992, but it may have existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Bosnian Muslim Green Berets, the entity also formed by the SDA, do you know the length of time that it existed and operated in the Bosnia-Herzegovina and Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if it existed beyond the time period of April 1992 through September 1992?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Let me just -- you've asked about Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Prijedor municipality. I can affirm that it existed in Bosnia-Herzegovina until at least April 1992. And I just don't know if it existed at all in Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know because we don't have or you haven't reviewed the minutes from the SDA executive board. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I just don't know, and I'm sure there are many documents that could enlighten us about that. Principally would be the records of the military organisation of the parties Republican level offices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask, sir, to review such records; namely, the records of the military organisation of the party's republic level offices?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you consider that those materials may shed some light on the Prijedor municipality, dependent upon whether or not the national defence council or the Bosnian Muslim Green Berets participated in any way in that municipality?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: They might.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would they, sir?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: They might, if they exist and if there are either a record of specific activity or no record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also mention one other entity called the Patriotic League. That was also formed by the SDA. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was also in mid -- I believe you said -- 1991, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I think the date can be assigned to May of 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know how long that entity, the Patriotic League, existed from the time of its inception, May of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: The Patriotic League ceased to exist as a distinct organisation on 15 April, 1992 when it was brought under the unified command of the Territorial Defence of the republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Probably can identify elements of it fighting as specific units, and I speak not of Prijedor here but particularly the Sarajevo area for the next couple of months anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The unified command of the Territorial Defence, did that membership consist of only one ethnic group in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No. The unified command of the Territorial Defence force consisted of a commander, who was a Bosnian Muslim, a deputy commander, who was a Bosnian Serb, another deputy commander, who was a Bosnian Croat, and the membership of the Territorial Defence force-at-large was, I would say, substantially a majority Muslims but included substantial numbers also of Serbs and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Territorial Defence in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did that also encompass activities within the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it, in fact, it being the Territorial Defence, encompassed all one 109 municipalities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't know that it took place in every municipality, but in certainly the vast majority of municipalities, there were Territorial Defence forces which were activated and played some role in the events of 1991 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the commander was of the Territorial Defence in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I can't recall, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Sefer Halilovic in any way a member of, or participant in the Territorial Defence in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: He was its commander at some point close to the 15th of April. I am not certain he was the first, but was its commander into, I think, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that this Mr. Halilovic was also the leader of the Patriotic League that we were just previously discussing?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: From about October 1991 onward, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Mr. Sefer Halilovic is, correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he still alive?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he claimed, or perhaps you don't but you'll let me know, that he claimed having in excess of 100.000 soldiers in his command when he was the leader of the patriotic league in 1991? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that claim, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of a claim that he had more or less, or you just don't know the number?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well, he wrote a book of memoirs and I think gave a number for 1992 of 60 or 70.000. I'm not aware of any claim anywhere near that size for 1991 but would not rule that out. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, did you review in any detail, or in any fashion, Sefer Halilovic's memoirs?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, I read his memoirs maybe two years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not Mr. Halilovic states that in 1992, he had in his command, in excess of 250.000 Bosnian Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, that Mr. Sefer Halilovic is under indictment here at this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you come to learn that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I follow the periodical press, both in the U.S. And former Yugoslavia, and came to that information at the time that he was -- the indictment was made public and he turned himself in to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Have you been able to -- or did you request any documents from the Office of the Prosecutor in connection with the indictment and Mr. Halilovic as it may relate to the Bosnia-Herzegovina and Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you, sir, think that examining the documents that may exist from the patriotic league and the Bosnian Muslim Green Berets and the national defence council may, indeed, be relevant to have a complete and thorough picture of the situation in the Prijedor municipality in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: It might be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to think that it wouldn't be?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Prior to examining them, I couldn't make that determination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we briefly discussed the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, where you mentioned that Mr. Izetbegovic was the president, and then you proceeded to discuss that the Territorial Defence consisted of a commander who was Muslim, a deputy who was Serbian, and then you also mentioned a Croatian in that spot. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the Muslims, Serbs, and Croatians at that time period, namely, June of 1991, operated under what I think you've identified as an inter- or intra-party agreement?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I think you've inaccurately characterised my earlier testimony. I identified the tri-party command structure of the unified Territorial Defence in April of 1992. In 1991, the defence -- the Territorial Defence structure was completely different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1991, was it true that the commander of the Territorial Defence was a Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear or do you know of any information which has led you to believe that the SDA party also or that the SDA party had their own Territorial Defence structure set up?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I think that's not the case. I believe I attempted to describe this relationship in my direct testimony and noted that the Territorial Defence force, as it existed at the end of the socialist period and into 1991, reported to the national defence organisation of the republic. But as 1991 went along, the Territorial Defence forces in each municipality often fell under the control of the nationalist party that was predominant in that municipality, or in some cases, remained loyal to the -- whatever, two parties together constituted a majority. So the influence of the let's say republic-level command diminished substantially in the course of 1991 as this trifurcation of the TO took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're familiar, because you obviously set forth some examples of the inter-party agreement. Correct, you're familiar with that agreement?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I wish I were more familiar with it. It's a series of verbal agreements as far as I am able to determine among the leaders of the three nationalist parties dating from the time of the election campaign into early 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to spend some time or at least have a better understanding and ask you some questions on the inter-party agreement but I forgot just one area that goes back to the other subject matter. So if I may, isn't it true, sir, that the SDS party in June of 1991 did not have the entity such as the equivalent in the SDA party, namely, the national defence council, the Bosnian Muslim Green Berets, and the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't know of any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the minutes that you reviewed from the SDS party at no time indicated that they were adopting or calling or founding, as you put it, entities such as those three that we've just previously identified, the national council -- national defence council, Bosnian Muslim Green Berets, and the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this intra-party agreement that you discussed --

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Excuse me. May I just respond to that question. You said at no time, and I would want to correct my answer, please, if I could, to say not in the time period that you are asking about, to be 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what time period did they exist?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: The military organisation of the SDS took place in the spring of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give me a month, sir?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well, we see evidence of it in -- let's see, April and May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any concrete evidence, sir, that the SDS party formed an entity such as the Bosnian Muslim Green Berets, a paramilitary unit, in the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, I believe there is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show that to us which are in the minutes under Tab 12 in the documents that you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Okay. It's going to take a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, I would ask...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I suggest in order to save time that we come back to this question after the next break.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, within the materials that you've provided to us indicating that you reviewed the -- some of the minutes of the SDS municipal board or assembly, can you tell us whether or not this is a complete category of all such SDS municipal board meetings?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: The volume principally in question, which makes up Exhibit 12, Tab 12, is a sequentially numbered bound volume. So there are -- presumably all minutes that were taken in this period are incorporated in this volume for minutes of 1991 as the volume is labelled. There may be other minutes of other sessions. As I indicated earlier, certain bodies which were not specifically the SDS municipal board were also included in the minutes in this volume, just two or three of them. So it's certainly feasible that other such bodies may have met, or that the SDS municipal board may have met and minutes taken in some other document or not taken at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do any of the minutes that you reviewed on Tab Number 12 indicate that there was a vote on any particular issues from the minutes starting with March 20th, 1991 through those in June -- of February 1992?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you identify those for us. If it will take awhile, we can come back to it at the break, if I may suggest that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I would point to two that are immediately identifiable. One is the 17th of September, 1991, on -- this is on -- the ERN is in English Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 00916407, about -- well, the fourth paragraph on this page. "With regard to the functioning of the assembly, two distinctive options have been brought up: One, not to take part in the assembly, one vote in favour. And two, take part in the assembly, obstruct its work, and keep the discussion aligned with the arguments we stated and with our press release. Others are in favour, 27." Then at the meeting on the 11th of September, 1991 at ERN 00916399, and 00916400, there are two votes, one for the president of the Prijedor municipal board of the SDS at the bottom of that first page, and votes for the vice-president continuing at the bottom of that page and on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any others that you can find?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm sure there are others. I would be very hard pressed to lay my hands on them in the course of the time that is available to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view that there are approximately 30 or so entries or minutes, if you will, of these various assemblies including the deputies' club. The one that you referenced most recently, September 11th, 1991, and when I say "most recently," I mean most recently in your testimony, that was the meeting Dr. Stakic was elected vice-president?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that at that meeting the SDA party president, I believe it's the late Muhamed Cehajic was also present, correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes. As I indicated, this was a public meeting. There were press representatives present and representatives of other political parties, including Mr. Cehajic and a representative of the social democratic party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Cehajic spoke at that September 11th, 1991 meeting and congratulated the parties for their concept of unity and openness, true?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I think he congratulated the party and said he was impressed with the degree of organisation. That's available on -- he also praised the very well-chosen entertainment on page 00916400.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 6400, can you point to me where Mr. Cehajic says that he is impressed with the degree of organisation?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well, let's look at his statement. Professor Muhamed Cehajic, president of the municipal assembly also wished to speak. He noted with pleasure the fine organisation of the assembly session and the very well-chosen entertainment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than that sentence, is there anywhere else in any of the documents that would support that Mr. Cehajic stated that he was "impressed" with this fine organisation?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I submit to you that the statement here is a good -- I mean it seems to be a good representation of his pleasure with the fine organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you take that to mean when he says "fine organisation" that he's impressed with their organisation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: He noted it with pleasure, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, when you reviewed these documents on Tab 12, did you note at which meetings Dr. Stakic was not present?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell from any of these exhibits on Tab 12 when Dr. Stakic may have been present and when he was not present?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: On most of them, one can make that determination. He was largely not present at these meetings from what I can see in the notes prior to late August of 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say he was largely not present, is it fair to say that in the majority of the meetings, that at least you've reviewed, these 30 or so, Dr. Stakic was not even present. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Until late August at which point his presence is apparent at most meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Late August of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can direct your attention to the September 17th, 1991, minutes of the SDS Prijedor municipal board meeting, that, sir, I believe was approximately one week after the election of Dr. Stakic's as vice-president, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, if you could give us an understanding, was there tension and friction between the various multiethnic parties, meaning between the SDA, the SDS, and the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: There was disagreement on fundamental issues between the nationalist parties. And I don't know that I would want to characterise that as friction or tension at that point. I probably am not able, on the basis of what I see, to so characterise it. But there was difference on fundamental issues that came to expression in the meetings of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to state that if we even reviewed the September 17th, 1991, SDS minutes the late Dr. Milan Kovacevic states that "the SDA is, after all, a party partner of ours." Do you recall reading that entry?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you think, sir, that there was no tension between the SDS and the SDA at that time, given what the SDS membership was voicing at their meetings?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well, I would say that he -- this was the same time, within one day, in which Dr. Stakic and Mr. Kovacevic led the walkout from the meeting of the executive committee of the Prijedor municipality. So one certainly would not say there was no disagreement at this time, and furthermore, that walkout clearly heightened the tension among the nationalist parties in September 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When in September 1991 did this walkout occur?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I would have to check, but either the 17th or 18th of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reason for the walkout, sir, are you familiar with the basis --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, would you please make a pause.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, they are referred to somewhat obliquely here, and more expressly in the press coverage of the event. The SDS leadership accused the SDA of failing to honour the inter-party agreement and to protest this failure, walked out of the municipal session. We, I think, then see the statement by Mr. Kovacevic and for that matter, Mr. Milan Pilipovic on page 00916405, that it was the SDS's desire to keep dialogue going even while they accused the SDA of having not honoured the inter-party agreement. So their determination to remain in the assembly and at the same time obstruct its work was consistent with their understanding of the SDA's failure to honour the inter-party agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, sir, at any time analyse whether or not. As you put it, the SDS leadership's accusation that the SDA failed to honour the intra-party agreement, did you ever determine if the SDS was correct in making that allegation or incorrect?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: On the basis of the -- examining the earlier decisions, I believe that accusation was partly true and partly not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which part was true and which was not true?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: The part that was true was that the SDA had filled on, an allegedly temporary basis, the position of the chief of the police station in Prijedor with a man who won denunciation in fact by Mr. Kovacevic on this very page. That interim appointment, however, was not yielded up to the SDS, as the SDS believed it ought to have. And at the same time, several of the appointments, or at least one of the appointments, to which the SDS referred -- SDS leaders referred to at this time was agreed upon by the party's prior leadership in January of 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you're familiar with the inter-party agreement, are you not?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: As I indicated, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also you set forth in your annex or addendum to your report, you have a discussion on the inter-party agreement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Inter-party agreement, sir, worked at both the republic level as well as the municipal level. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well, it didn't work at either level. It worked at, let us say, the highest levels of government to divide the major governing portfolios. But when it came to discussions about mid-level governing appointments, appointments in educational institutions, various institutes, enterprises, the terms of the inter-party agreement were sufficiently unclear and, in many cases, subject to other considerations that the failure to fulfill this agreement on the part of all nationalist parties was uniformly difficult at these lower levels of government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you point to any material that you have reviewed which shows that the SDA complained that the SDS failed to fulfill this agreement at any level?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that with you?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I believe there is reference -- I'm not going to be able to find it in the next four hours, so...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: But there were many, many such complaints at the republic level and numerous complaints at the level of Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that in the Prijedor municipality, the chief complaint that commenced the exacerbation of tensions was the breach by the SDA of the inter-party agreement by failing to give, as previously agreed, the position of commander of police station in Prijedor to a person of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who, can you tell us, in the municipality of Prijedor, of the top functions, as you call them or offices, can you tell us how the inter-party agreement worked? Who got which positions and start with the president.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: You're going to test my memory sorely unless I can refer to the report. The president of the Prijedor municipal assembly was designated by the SDA, and that was Mr. Cehajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, can I make an objection at this point. Is an area which one is in the report, two is covered in the examination-in-chief, and all the witness is now doing is simply rehearsing for the third time in front of you the contents of a report of which you're already aware. It is, in my respectful submission, wasting time, and I would suggest that counsel be asked to move on and actually simply cross-examine him on this rather simply asking him to repeat as I say for the third time evidence that is already available to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained. And before coming to the break, whenever, and it's true for both parties, until now I showed a lot of patience. Whenever you want to make reference to former statements, and you are aware that this issue was already addressed by the witness, please be so kind and quote to the record the page you're referring to, and only then it will be possible to identify, if you want to do so, discrepancies. But I will not allow to repeat and repeat the same issues already discussed in the past. Of course, as I said, it's for you, if you regard -- if you believe that there are discrepancies, then you can come back. But only by quoting the former statement in full. Let's have a break now until 5.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Before we continue with the cross-examination, is it correct that the 92 bis project is finalized and the OTP is prepared to present the entire documents to the record?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: For the record, the documents are before the Prosecutor's table, and we are prepared to hand them over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then it's -- there is a general possibility to read these documents and then we have now the seven days's time limit. This brings us to the 1st of May. The 1st of May, we will discuss and take into account the objections by the Defence on this issue. Before we ask Dr. Donia to come in, the Trial Chamber has decided the following, taking into account the already formally stated limited probative value of an expert witness when it's on the individual criminal responsibility, taking into account that the Defence counsel has already on several occasions been warned to concentrate on the major and important issues, there is only time until 7.00 sharp for the finalisation of the cross-examination. May the expert witness be brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, a couple questions to follow up on this issue of disagreement between the SDA and the SDS, it involved, among others, as you've stated, the appointment of commander of the police station in Prijedor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who, ultimately, sir, can make such an appointment as the appointment of commander of the police station in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm not certain who has that. The ultimate authority would have, certainly in socialist times, lay with the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In socialist times, the Minister of Interior? In 1991 or 1992, you don't know which body. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: It's not clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may, just a couple more questions on the minutes that are reflected in tab Number 12 of the volume before you. Generally speaking, the minutes that you've reviewed were unsigned. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I think that some of them were signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why I said generally speaking. Some were signed, some were not. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, as I recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with, what in the United States of America governing bodies rely on, as the Robert's rules of order. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that but have not mastered them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with conducting meetings that Robert's rules of record requires that the next meeting, that the minutes of the prior meeting be read and accepted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you really believe that the Robert's rules of record are accepted in former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to make my point and I'll go further, I'm trying to just show the lack of -- I don't want to give an argument on it. If you want, I can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know if at any time the minutes of these meetings were reviewed by any of the members who were participants in those meetings?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the accuracy is of the secretary or the individual who was keeping the minutes of those meetings were?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well, I generally assess it as good but not precise. The minutes are filled with incomplete sentences, summaries of statements, occasional quotes, and then a general characterisation often of a presentation in one or two sentences of a speech or presentation that may have lasted several minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that some of the minutes that you reviewed actually identify the time the meeting started and the time in which the meeting ended? Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in some instances, those meetings that you've reviewed on Tab 12 lasted several hours?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And out of those several-hour discussions, if you will, at this SDS meeting, the person who was recording them couldn't have possibly recorded verbatim what each individual said. Isn't that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention to another topic, if you will, although strictly confined to the Prijedor municipality, are you familiar, sir, with what functions or posts were placed within Prijedor of four different municipalities in the surrounding area of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I know that there were several, and one of them was, for example, the medical services in the area. And there were a couple of others that were there, and I can't recall exactly what they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This director of medical services, who appointed that individual?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who had the authority to appoint that individual, do you know?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when that individual was appointed?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well, there was an incumbent at the time of the elections, and I don't know at what point that incumbent was replaced, if at all, during this period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I mention some other posts or functions that were placed in Prijedor by these four municipalities, and you would be kind enough just to tell me if you believe they were included in this or not: Commander of the traffic police, or police of traffic?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The director of public health?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I think we're speaking of the same position of the director of medical services.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it, sir, your understanding the director of medical services and director of public health is one and the same position?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm not positive. No, I'm not sure that's the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the director of the public accounting services? Is that one of the posts that were filled in Prijedor by these four municipalities immediately after the election?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the director of elektroprenos?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the position of the director of the PTT, which is the post, telegram, and telephone, I believe, whether that position falls within the area of Prijedor which was governed by four different municipalities?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for the director of medical services and the director of the PTT, you're sure of those two. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm confident that those were positions based in Prijedor that were -- that operated by agreement among these -- the Prijedor and neighbouring municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were those neighbouring municipalities?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Again, I think I'd have to refer to my report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may, maybe if I give you the name, you can disagree or agree with it. How about Bosanka Dubica?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Dubica, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about Bosanski Novi?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And obviously the municipality of Prijedor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Prijedor municipality at that time was divided and its president was a member of the SDA. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: What time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when these posts were being filled after the election in 1991.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I can't agree with your characterisation that the Prijedor municipality at that time was divided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the Prijedor municipality at that time which consisted of the majority of three multi-ethnic parties, were they unified?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: In some matters, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in others, they were not?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they unified, sir, in agreeing between the other three municipalities that we've listed, Bosanska Dubica, Bosanski Novi and Sanski Most to have the seat of the posts that I have read, although admittedly two of which you're confident, that they have agreed with these other municipalities? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, I don't believe that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Prijedor municipality objected to these posts being in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who disagreed, then? The other municipalities?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: As I understand it, from the evidence I've looked at, there was disagreement among the municipalities and among the parties in the various municipalities. So, this subject of filling these posts was a topic of complex negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, it was ultimately resolved?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't think it was resolved until June of 1992 when the SDS took all the positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We discussed September 1991. We examined some minutes, and we discussed other items, the inter-party agreement as it related to various positions in that time period. In 1991, September, was it also a period where the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina ordered the mobilisation of its men?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Of its what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Men.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a mobilisation in September of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who ordered it?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence force in Prijedor ordered a mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was on this Territorial Defence force in Prijedor who ordered this mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well, the commander was named Javoric and was essentially the person in charge of that mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the men respond to that mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: There was a substantial response, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, wasn't this mobilisation a deployment to western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Preparation for a deployment to western Slavonia, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, when you say that there was substantial response, there was substantial response from all three multi-ethnic entities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: There was the greatest response came from those of Serbian nationality, but there was substantial response from all three groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a per cent of a whole, did you ever quantify what percentage was Serbian, Muslim, or Croatian?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: There are a number of references to those divisions, and I'm not too sure that either one of them or any of them are quite the mobilisation unit concerned. It also was the case that the person who subsequently reported the casualties from this mobilisation showed that there was a -- there were members of the three ethnicities who perished in that battle or on that battle front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Prijedor municipal assembly which had as its president Muhamed Cehajic, did they address this mobilisation issue at any of its meetings?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they merely have discussions regarding this mobilisation, or did it have to be authorised and voted upon?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Well this, what I've called the first mobilisation, was in fact kicked over to the National Defence Council of the municipality. And a meeting was held of the National Defence Council. And at that meeting, the SDA representatives indicated that the mobilisation was authorised by the republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they, sir, or did they not at the Prijedor municipal assembly in September of 1991 unanimously vote in agreement in an approval of the mobilisation call?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't recall that they did, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned this was the first mobilisation, and obviously there was another one in November of 1991. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second mobilisation, if you will, was it also a request for all multi-ethnic parties to join for this mobilisation and deployment?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: As I indicated in the paper, it was a compromise resolution that passed unanimously in the municipal assembly on the 7th of November. That resolution, which was subsequently echoed in the mobilisation call, required that all persons subject to mobilisation report to the local base, that those who wished to deploy back to Croatia could do so, and that those who did not wish to deploy were required to turn in their weapons and allowed to return to their homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it true as a result of this compromise resolution that was passed unanimously in the Prijedor municipal assembly that, in fact, the majority of Muslim and Croats did not become mobilised and did not join forces with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: This statement of fact is true, I agree. It was a result of this resolution and other factors that had in the meantime alienated the vast majority of Muslims and Croats from the idea of fighting with the JNA in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned briefly who appointed the chief of the police station in Prijedor. Do you know, sir, who appointed or appoints the deputy of the chief of police -- of police station in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm not clear what that position is. The idea is that the chief of police was an appointment that would be nominated by the leading party. The chief of the police station, which was sometimes also referred to as the "deputy" was appointed by the second ranking nationalist party. Does that answer your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It doesn't, but that's fine. If I may proceed. Is there a subordinate to the chief of the police station that has a function?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact this inter-party agreement, the parties had agreed prior to the election that the party who wins, has the majority, will select or nominate chief of police, and the second-place party will be given the position of the chief of the police station. Correct? Among others, of course?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Focussing just on those two, and if we can just focus on that, did the SDA object to the nominee that the SDS had for chief of the police station following the elections and having the understanding of the inter-party agreements?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The SDA did not object to the SDS's nominee for that position?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: The objection came from the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the Minister of Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time? Was he a member of the SDS party?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't recall just offhand who was -- I do recall that two representatives of the Ministry of the Interior came up to Prijedor at that time. One was, I believe, Montila Mandic [phoen], and the other I can't recall without referring to the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think, sir, that the party of the SDA held the position of Minister of the Interior at that time?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we know clearly that it wasn't the SDS representative at that post of Minister of Interior; it was an SDA representative from the Minister of Interior who objected to the nominee by the SDS for that position, chief of police station?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is not clear from the record that I examined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Alija Delimustafic?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: He was a leader of the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, as a leader of the SDA party, what position or post he held at the time we're discussing?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm not certain, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you -- strike that. Do you know that, in fact, Mr. Delimustafic was the Minister of Interior during this time?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I just don't recall specifically, but I would accept your representation if that's what you're representing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving to another issue, if you can please have Exhibit Number SK46A in front of you. I have just a couple questions on this. And if I can just, for the record, state that it has a date stamp number 01107302.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: You said 46A? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I have, yes. You have that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I have that document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just to clear so -- so we're clear we're talking of the same document, does it not have next to the word "translation" the date stamp 01107302?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: This is a precis or summary of minutes of the SDS municipal board meeting of 9 May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you briefly mentioned in your direct that Dr. Stakic was present at that meeting. Correct? If I can direct your attention to speed it up, second page, halfway down. See his name mentioned there?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, sir, the person who took these minutes and writes under Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Dr. Stakic's name that "as of May 9th, 1992, Dr. Stakic advocated peace instead of war for the region," and he states that "peace must be maintained at all costs." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You relied on this document as well, did you not, sir, in formulating your report that we previously marked as SK43?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any reason, sir, that we should doubt the veracity of the person recording these notes as they being attributed to Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We accept them as being true -- strike that. Do you accept them as being true, sir?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Within the confines of the general reservations I expressed earlier about the character of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may just have a moment, Your Honour, to consult.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Donia. Your Honour, we have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May we now come to the re-examination first. Re-examined by Mr. Cayley:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, during your cross-examination you were asked during a considerable period about the completeness of your report and your evidence to this Trial Chamber. Do you recall that cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that the Office of the Prosecutor does not have any minutes from the reformist party? Did you know that, the reformist party in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour, because the question assumes facts not in evidence. If my learned friend is going to testify, that's fine. It's just inappropriate to ask that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, reformulate your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, Dr. Donia, as to whether or not the Office of the Prosecutor has the reform party minutes in its possession?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: I am not aware, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen the reform party minutes from the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware whether or not the Office of the Prosecutor has within its possession the SDS -- the SDA minutes from the municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have they ever been offered to you?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware as to whether or not the Office of the Prosecutor has within its possession the HDZ minutes, the HDZ party minutes, from the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, speaking of the completeness of your report, have you ever put together a report where you have had at your disposal every single piece of material that could be possibly relevant to that particular report that you're putting together? Any piece of work you've ever done?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you cite to any example of any piece of historical work that you know of, by any historian where that historian has had at his disposal every piece of material that could be relevant to the piece of work that he is writing?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a reality, isn't it, Dr. Donia, that in historical research, not every piece of material that could be relevant to that report is available to the person putting that report together, isn't it? It's a fact of life.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: That's always true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And bearing in mind in the report, what you've just said, the report that you produced in respect to the municipality of Prijedor, bearing in mind it is always true that you never have all of the material that you would want at your disposal, do you still maintain that your report that you produced is an accurate opinion on the material that you had available to you at the time?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, you were asked a number of questions about the Patriotic League and the Green Berets. What was the military force of the Bosnian Serbs in Bosnia? What was that called?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. I don't have a time frame, so I'm not sure what time frame possibly this witness could answer since he didn't give us a time frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: In --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please repeat, taking into account this objection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May of 1992, what was the military force of the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: On May 12th, 1992, the military force of the Bosnian Serbs became the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what military units was the VRS composed?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: It was made up of units of the Yugoslav national army, the JNA, that were in Bosnia at that time. And that included its vast majority of its personnel and the vast majority of its weaponry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you were to make a basic qualitative judgment of the JNA, as opposed to the Green Berets and the Patriotic League, who was the most powerful military force in Bosnia in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question, Your Honour, on two bases. As I mentioned form also, it's not set forth. Is it a new opinion, I'm asking counsel, we'd like to know the basis of it is. And again, I would ask with the prior question that there's no time frame put on this. Two questions prior, my learned friend did put May of 1992, although he was discussing purportedly my cross-examination questions dealing with the Bosnian Muslim Green Berets and the Patriotic League, which were clearly defined in each of my questions as 1991. But I certainly on these three bases would object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Dismissed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could go back to the question that I asked you, could you please make a basic qualitative judgment of who was the most powerful military force when comparing the VRS and the Green Berets and Patriotic League in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: By far the most powerful military force in Bosnia in May 1992 was the JNA, which then on 12 May transformed itself into the Bosnian Serb army. This was particularly true of the relative weight of weaponry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to read very briefly from a section of your original report, Prosecutor's Exhibit 43. And I don't wish you to refer to it so we can move through this quickly, but it is on page 56 of your original report in the Brdjanin/Talic case. And it is a part of the report that is referring to the role of the JNA. And I will read the final paragraph on page 56: "In the transfer of armed forces into nationalist hands, the decisive role was played by the JNA. In summer 1991, the JNA distributed weapons, mostly small arms and mobile weapons, to TO units in Serb-majority municipalities and to local committees of the SDS."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. My learned friend could just direct me to the page number again. I had trouble following it, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Page 56, at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Starts with ARK assembly accorded itself the right?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Prosecutor's Exhibit 43.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we can deal with this -- do you want me to give you the page? If you could give counsel the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have Prosecutor's Exhibit SK 43, Your Honour. I'm looking at it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This is the report from Brdjanin/Talic, not the Prijedor report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have SK 43. I have page 56, Your Honour, the amended Prijedor report was much thinner. So it's just not on my page. I don't know if it is on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'll give you my copy, and you can read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Again, my problem with, that Your Honour, is I'm not sure if the Court has the report, and why don't we have it if I'm looking at page 56 and that's the report that's the exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could you hand to me the report, and I'll find it for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Here's page 56.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: The summaries my learned friend has is a version that has been paginated differently. In his version, it's on page 59.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I thank both parties for their cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I apologise for that. I don't know how that happened. But we will find out. I don't know how you have a version that has been paginated differently from this version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyway, if I could ask you the question, Dr. Donia: Is it right that the JNA played a decisive role in the transfer of armed forces in nationalist hands?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the JNA distribute arms for Muslims and Croats in Bosnia in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your view that the formation of the Green Berets and the Patriotic League was a response to the distribution of arms by the JNA, to the Serb population?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: In part, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your cross-examination, you referred to the minutes of the 17th of September of 1991 as an example of where voting took place. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look very briefly at those minutes again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And this, Your Honours, is on page 00916407.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, I have that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is the section which you quoted in response to the question where Slavko Safic is stating with regard to the functioning of the assembly, two distinctive options have been brought up. Can you explain to the Judges the two options that were brought up, the significant of those options, and explain why the second was, in fact, adopted, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: This debate within the SDS about whether to participate in the legislative bodies at the Republican level and the municipal level was an ongoing discussion. And in this case, the party in Prijedor is following the lead of the SDS organisation in Bosnia-Herzegovina more generally to continue to participate even with occasional walkouts and to, thereby, have a -- let's say both an ear and a voice in those representative bodies. But essentially to obstruct where possible their decision-making capability. My view of this decision at this time, goes along with the walkout of the executive committee on approximately the same day and the determination to become much more critical, confrontational, with the SDA regarding the inter-party agreement. So from this point on, the participation of the SDS in the assembly sessions became much more contingent, less designed to produce a fruitful outcome of the ongoing talks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The word "obstruct" is recorded in the minutes, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to characterise this as essentially the SDS stating "We'll appear to participate, but in reality, we want our way and our arguments, and we'll obstruct where necessary" would that be a characterisation you would agree with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this mischaracterisation. My learned friend is taking a simple statement and completely distorting it. And if we just look several paragraphs down when M. Kovacevic speaks, there's a different view. So I'm not sure why, with respect to the Court's prior comments on time -- I didn't discuss this issue, he has given it in cross, he has discussed it ad nauseum.
